messages:
Nikki H.: quick async check — I'm about to land the patch that adds `model_hint` and `route_tier` to /v1/generate. want a sanity pass on the contract and backward compatibility notes.

Tom R.: thanks — can you paste the request/response example? curious how fallback interplay is expressed.

Nikki H.: sure. current plan: user can send either `model_id` (strong) or `model_hint` (soft). routing will prefer `model_id` if present. `model_hint` + `route_tier`/`region_hint` are routing suggestions only, not hard pins. example: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_hint": "rw-phi-1b",
  "model_id": "rw-phi-1b-q4",
  "route_tier": "standard",
  "region_hint": "eu-west-1",
  "input": "Summarize the doc"
}
```
response will include `served_model` (id actually used) and `fallback_used`: boolean. if `model_id` is incompatible with request shape we either return 400 (if incompatible) or fallback to a compatible variant and set `fallback_used`: true and `fallback_reason`.

Sahil: couple quick questions — 1) what does "incompatible with request shape" mean here? sequence length only, or also special tokenization/model family mismatch? 2) if someone omits both `model_id` and `model_hint` we fall back to catalog default right?

Nikki H.: good q. shape = model family + tokenization + max_seq. We validate: if `model_id` belongs to a family that doesn't support streaming and the request asked for `stream: true`, we treat as incompatible. For tokenization-family mismatches (e.g., different vocab), we err on the safe side and 400 unless the system knows a lossless mapping.

Elaine: small clarifying point on defaults: yes — no model fields => route to tenant-default model (same as today). `route_tier` defaults to `standard`. Also, we won't change the old response fields; `served_model` is additive.

Tom R.: what about semantics of `route_tier`: is it strict? e.g., user requests `premium` but only `standard` available in region — do we downgrade? or return 409?

Nikki H.: non-strict. policy: try exact tier in preferred region, then same tier other region, then lower tier (if user allowed fallback). we surface `serving_path` and `fallback_stack` arrays in `served_meta` to make audit easy. if user sets `tier_strict=true` we'll return 409 on mismatch.

Sahil: sdk implications — should SDK surface `served_model` and warnings? i'd propose a top-level `served_model` plus `debug.serving_path` in the response. SDK should warn if `fallback_used`.

Elaine: docs note: add a compatibility table listing common incompat checks (streaming vs non-streaming, embeddings-only models, kv-cache size). Also add quick sample for canary: `model_hint` + `fallback_models` list for safe rollouts.

Nikki H.: deploying a canary flag first: rollout flag `model_routing_v2` -> off by default. will enable for internal orgs, then customers. plan: merge API change behind flag, update SDKs, then flip flag.

Tom R.: can deploy-bot run a quick smoke that posts a request with `model_hint` only and ensure response includes `served_model`? also check header `x-served-model` for backward compat with infra logs.

deploy-bot: scheduled smoke on staging in 5m. test case: POST /v1/generate {"model_hint":"rw-phi-1b","input":"hi","region_hint":"us-west-2"} -> expect 200 + `served_model` in body + `x-served-model` header. will post results. :robot_face:

Sahil: last ask — make sure the OpenAPI spec keeps `200` schema backward compatible: mark `served_model` as nullable string (so old clients ignore). add `deprecated` flags only where absolutely necessary.

Nikki H.: noted. thanks all. i'll update the PR with doc snippets and the OpenAPI diff. please ping here if you see anything risky. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: smoke complete — staging ✅. served_model present: "rw-phi-1b-q4"; header present. no errors observed.
